messages: You strike Dr. Zaun down before he can say another word.
The way to the escape route is now open.

intro: Z A U N   B I O M E D I C A L
You wake on an examination table with no memory of the last 72 hours.
A nurse named Emily is nearby. The facility is dark, sealed, and overrun.
Somewhere beyond the lobby, Dr. Zaun is still inside.

rooms.description:
EXAM ROOM
Cold fluorescent lights buzz above the table where you woke up.
A broken bottle, flashlight, bandages, and Emily's notebook are nearby.
The only exit is north.

npcs.name: emily
npcs.description:
A nurse in bloodstained scrubs.
She is scared, exhausted, and still trying to help. Try 'talk to emily'.

dialogues.text:
Emily grips your arm before you can stand.
'Don't move too fast. You were in bad shape when I found you.' She glances toward the door.
'The generator is dead - no power means no security systems, no locked doors, and no way to access the research terminal in the east wing. We need fuel. I saw a canister in the research lab before things went wrong.'
She pauses, voice dropping.
'And if you run into Dr. Zaun - don't engage. Don't listen to what he says. Just walk away.'

hints: Before leaving, check the supplies and read Emily's notebook. It explains how to survive.

rooms.description:
CENTRAL LOBBY
The reception desk is torn apart and the monitors are dead.
A reinforced door blocks the north wing.
Exits lead east, west, and south.

enemies.name: standard infected
enemies.description:
A slow infected guard shambles through the lobby.
It looks weak, but it will attack if ignored. A sharp item should work.

hints: An infected is active here. Deal with immediate danger before trying to read, take, or use anything.
The north door is locked. The east and west rooms look like the next places to investigate.

rooms.description:
RESEARCH LAB
Files and broken terminals cover the floor in careful piles.
Fuel, research notes, and scrap metal stand out in the mess.
A security terminal waits on the wall.

enemies.name: clicker
enemies.description:
A blind infected researcher clicks softly to map the room.
Its sealed eyes make it vulnerable to sudden light.

interactables.name: terminal
interactables.description:
A cracked security terminal for the north wing door.
It needs power first. After the generator is running, try 'use terminal'.
interactables.successMessage:
The terminal shudders to life as the power comes back online.
The Zaun Biomedical logo flashes once, then dissolves into a single prompt:
> NORTH WING ACCESS - CLEARANCE CODE REQUIRED
Type 'enter code <code>' once you know the full code.
interactables.failureMessage:
The terminal is completely dead.
Without power to the facility, it's just a cracked screen and a faded logo.
interactables.forbiddenMessage: The terminal is already unlocked. The north wing door is open.

npcs.name: emily
npcs.description:
Emily searches the room for anything useful.
She may know what to do after the power comes back.

dialogues.text:
Emily keeps her voice barely above a whisper.
'The terminal is live. Zaun used a custom access code for the north wing - he didn't trust the standard facility protocols.'
She hesitates.
'I found fragments of it in the research records. Two numbers on separate pages. He split it deliberately. Read everything carefully'

Emily stares at the terminal screen without blinking.
When she finally speaks, her voice is hollow.
'NV-1 wasn't a failed experiment. It was never meant to heal anyone. Zaun built it to do exactly this - and then he stayed behind to watch.'
She looks at you.
'The door is open. He's waiting for you up there. Be careful. He wants you to walk through that door.'

hints: The clicking enemy reacts to light. Make the room safe before searching it.
This lab has fuel, notes, scrap metal, and a terminal that will matter once power returns.

rooms.description:
GENERATOR ROOM
Red emergency lights wash over a silent diesel generator.
The fuel gauge is empty.
The exit back to the lobby is east.

enemies.name: ripper
enemies.description:
A fast infected moves on all fours around the generator.
It looks too quick to outrun. A heavy strike may stop it.

interactables.name: generator
interactables.description:
A backup generator with an empty fuel intake.
If you have the fuel canister, try 'use generator'.
interactables.successMessage:
You twist the intake cap free and pour the fuel canister into the generator.
The machine coughs, kicks, and then catches - a deep mechanical growl that shakes the walls.
Overhead, the fluorescent lights stutter and flare to life.
Somewhere in the facility, something hums back to power.
interactables.failureMessage:
The generator won't start.
The fuel gauge reads completely empty - you need to find fuel first.

hints: The ripper makes working on the generator unsafe. Deal with it first.
The generator needs fuel before it can restore power.

rooms.description:
CONTAINMENT LABORATORY
Containment chambers line the walls in perfect order.
Dr. Zaun waits beside a huge amber tank.
The exit north is locked.

npcs.name: zaun
npcs.description:
Dr. Arlen Zaun, lead researcher on NV-1.
He is waiting for you to speak. Try 'talk to zaun'.

dialogues.text:
Zaun clasps his hands behind his back, the way a professor would at the front of a lecture hall.
'You made it further than any of the others. I had hoped you would.'
He glances at the containment chambers.
'You think NV-1 was an accident. A failure. I understand why - that is what the records were designed to suggest.'
A faint smile.
'This facility was never a hospital. It was a proof of concept. And you are standing in the results.'

Zaun hasn't moved from his position near the tank.
He watches the chaos with the calm of someone observing a controlled experiment - which, you realize, is exactly what this is to him.

Zaun surveys the stillness of the room. The bodies of his subjects. The shattered chambers.
He looks almost satisfied.
'Remarkable. Every single one.'
He turns to face you fully for the first time.
'I did not build a fail-safe into this facility. I built a selection mechanism. You are what survives.'
He spreads his hands.
'So. What do you do with that?'

hints: Zaun is waiting. Speaking to him will move things forward.
The enemy notes still matter here. After the danger is over, you will need to decide what to do.

rooms.description:
EXIT ROOM
A narrow emergency corridor ends at a sealed fire escape hatch.
A keycard reader blinks beside the handle.
The only exit back is south.

interactables.name: keycard
interactables.description:
A reinforced emergency exit hatch with a red keycard reader.
If you have Zaun's keycard, try 'use keycard'.
interactables.successMessage:
You press Zaun's keycard against the reader.
A beat of silence - then a heavy magnetic clunk as the lock releases. The hatch swings outward on its own weight.
Cold night air floods the corridor, carrying the smell of smoke and rain and open sky.
Emily steps through first. You follow. Behind you, the hatch seals shut.
ENDING: SURVIVAL
interactables.failureMessage:
The reader blinks red.
The lock holds.
You need a high-clearance keycard to open this.

hints: The hatch needs a keycard. If you do not have one, the answer is behind you.

items.name: notebook
items.description:
Emily's notebook explains enemy weaknesses and contains part of a code.
Infected are slow: try 'stab infected' with a sharp item.
Clickers are blind: try 'flash clicker' with the flashlight.
Rippers are fast: try 'strike ripper' with something heavy.
Brutes need a better weapon: combine glass and metal, then stab.
A code fragment is underlined: 73xx.

items.name: flashlight
items.description:
A cracked tactical flashlight with a strong beam.
Useful against blind enemies. Try 'flash <enemy>' when needed.

items.name: bandages
items.description:
Sterile bandages from the exam room supply cart.
If you are wounded, try 'use bandages' before the next attack kills you.

items.name: research notes
items.description:
Research notes on NV-1 mutations.
They confirm light hurts blind subjects and heavy impacts can stop rippers.
A circled line says reinforced glass weapons work against brutes.
At the bottom, another code fragment is scrawled: 14.

items.name: fuel canister
items.description:
A sealed diesel canister from emergency storage.
Needed to restart the generator. Try 'use generator' in the generator room.

items.name: scrap metal
items.description:
A heavy strip of structural steel wrapped like a crude handle.
Useful as a weapon. Try 'strike <enemy>' or combine it with another item.

items.name: broken bottle
items.description:
A sharp broken reagent bottle.
Sharp but fragile. Try 'stab <enemy>' or combine it with scrap metal.

items.name: improvised blade
items.description:
A crude blade made from broken glass and scrap metal.
Strong enough for tougher infected. Try 'stab <enemy>'.

items.name: keycard
items.description:
A high-clearance security keycard taken from Zaun.
It should open the final emergency hatch. Try 'use keycard' in the exit room.

encounterPhases.message:
Zaun moves to the first containment column and enters a code without looking at the keypad.
He has done this before.
The chamber seals disengage with a pressurized hiss and three figures stumble forward - slow, broken, still wearing what they arrived in. Stage 1. Early infection.
He watches them the way you'd watch a timer run down.

Zaun turns to the next column without a word.
These chambers are darker.
The moment the seals release, the sound begins - a rapid, rhythmic clicking that fills the room like static. Two figures emerge.
Their faces are wrong: eye sockets sealed shut beneath fused scar tissue, heads tilting in sharp precise angles as they map the room by sound alone.
Stage 2.
He has been keeping them fed.

The final chamber is the largest.
The door is reinforced with additional bolts that Zaun unlocks one by one, methodically, like he is unwrapping something precious.
When it finally opens, the sound precedes the thing itself - a low, grinding drag of something massive moving on all fours.
It fills the doorframe.
What NV-1 does to most subjects in six days, it has done to this one completely. The bones restructured. The muscle density is extraordinary.
It does not hesitate.
